replacements.text: All right, have it your way. Heroically, you throw yourself onto your sword. Nothing happens! No blood, no pain, absolutely nothing! Frustrated, you try again. Still nothing. If only your girlfriend could see you now. You don't make an exit this stylish every day! Then it is over, and everything goes dark... Some time later, you wake to find yourself floating in a dark space. You shudder. Is this the afterlife? Is this really all there is? Not a bright prospect... Then you realise what woke you. A gentle voice drifts towards you, faint and distant. "Dave Parker!" it whispers. "You should know that no one can escape their destiny. Fleeing it is pointless: fate always catches up with you! Go and complete the tasks you have been given. By my divine authority, I grant you an extra life, and one more chance to fulfil your destiny..." As the voice fades, everything starts spinning. You grow dizzy and fall into a deep, dreamless sleep. When you open your eyes again, you are exactly where you tried to kill yourself...

Looking around, you get the impression the decorators were desperate to show how prosperous and worldly their little village is. Sadly, they tried rather too hard. replacements.text: You stand on the shore of Loch Calderwood, speechless at the view. Before you lies a picturesque mountain lake, ringed by high, jagged peaks behind which the sun is slowly setting. To the northwest, a waterfall roars down from the mountains. A dangerously romantic feeling comes over you, and you consider calling your girlfriend. Then you dismiss the idea. What chance would a soppy romantic have with the girls around here? Besides, you left your girlfriend at home for a reason, didn't you? A few lengths of the lake might be just the thing to get you in shape before you bestow your attentions on the ladies of Scotland. If you'd like a little exercise before your campaign of conquest, enter the lake to the north. Otherwise, the road south leads back to your hotel.

replacements.text: You can't help smiling as you enter the hotel dining room. One of them, an elderly man with a long beard, sits at a corner table studying the menu and savouring his beer. If you're hungry or thirsty, you could join him. Otherwise, you can leave through the door behind you.

replacements.text: As you wade west across the muddy lake bed, the water gets colder and deeper. Until now you could just about stand, but you're running out of bottom. Time to swim, unless you fancy sinking! "Oh well, it'll toughen me up!" you tell yourself. You splash a little water onto your heroic chest, then fling yourself forwards with magnificent disregard for your own survival. Brrr! For a summer evening, that water is cold! After a few seconds you get used to it. Quite pleasant, really. All that's missing is your rubber duck. As you make your first clumsy strokes, you feel a strong current pulling you south, towards a gigantic whirlpool that swallows anything careless enough to stray within reach. You can swim in any direction except west.

replacements.text: You are swimming in front of the waterfall at the northwest end of the lake. Struggling against the current, you wonder what might be behind that wall of water. You can swim back towards the middle of the lake, or try diving beneath the waterfall to discover what it hides...

replacements.text: Still dazed by the waterfall's battering, you struggle to keep afloat. Then you freeze in astonishment, promptly sink and swallow a mouthful of water! When you surface, the shock hits you: you're still on the south side of the waterfall! That alone might have a perfectly reasonable explanation. You did lose your bearings underwater. You could accept it if... if... if the village were still there! But it has vanished. Where the little settlement stood, a deep, dark forest now crowds the shore, full of trees you've never seen before. replacements.text: You climb onto the shore. The waterfall still rumbles in the southwest corner of the lake. You're less sure where your parents will imagine you are when you fail to call tonight. replacements.text: As politely as you can after that welcome, you ask for your key. After every sentence, the porter cups a hand behind his left ear. Apparently his hearing isn't quite as good as he thinks. Eventually he understands, takes your key from the board and tosses it onto the counter. "Room zero-zero-three," he mutters, then turns and shuffles upstairs. "Charming," you think. "No wonder nobody stays here!" Sadly, your silent wish that he might slip and tumble back down remains unfulfilled. Now, now! No need to get vicious. replacements.text: You beckon the waitress over and announce your most pressing needs: "A big steak, a cold beer and a Fra..." Suddenly you blush. "Er, forget the Frankfurter Allgemeine. You probably don't get German newspapers here anyway, do you?" The girl, equally red-faced, hurriedly says no. Ignoring the good ten years between you, you reassure her in a fatherly tone: "Never mind, my child. I can't speak German anyway!" You roar with laughter. The local, who has been minding his own business, rolls his eyes as though your joke has caught him squarely between the legs. Discovering that the waitress also suffers from a chronic lack of humour, you cut your performance short and dismiss her with a gracious wave. Once she has disappeared into the kitchen, you ask the old man about the village and its surroundings. He slowly mumbles into his beard that he knows an interesting legend. Fine. You weren't expecting a list of trendy nightspots and yuppie discos, but does it have to be a fairy tale? You prop your head on your hands, just in case you nod off and hit your nose on the table. Longing for your food so you'll at least have something to do, you listen. Long ago, a rich, proud city stood where Loch Calderwood lies today. In a single night it vanished, leaving a lake at the foot of the mountains! People said the gods had punished its inhabitants for their pride and vanity. They were said to be wealthy and wonderfully skilled craftsmen. You've been practising the art of sleeping with your eyes open, but the old man mistakes your stare for amazement and goes one better. Even now, the villagers claim you can see the city's towers and rooftops if you dive to the bottom of the lake at midnight under a full moon. replacements.text: The old man hides behind his beer glass, unable to get another word out. All you hear from time to time is a quiet, embarrassed "Burp!" Apparently he's had one too many during his story...

replacements.text: After recovering a little, the unicorn thanks you and earnestly warns you against continuing west. "Once you leave this part of the forest, there is no turning back..." It gives you the small, glowing ball and whispers in a fading voice, "Think of me when you use it. I do not have long to live..." The beautiful, doomed creature gives you one last look, so full of sorrow and pain that it almost breaks your heart. Then it turns and slowly walks away, never looking back, until it disappears among the trees...

Everything around you blurs! You stagger, then fall! The shock makes you drop the amulet. It rolls away out of sight, but at last its hypnotic spell is broken. With this sword in your hand, you feel ready to take on every power in the world. Well, we'll see whether that optimism is justified...

replacements.text: You cautiously take a puff on the orc father's pipe. Its sweet smoke carries you into another world, where you fly through the clouds in a customised, low-slung toaster and pink elephants direct the traffic. Suddenly, multicoloured raindrops start falling. Visibility in your turbo-toaster gets worse and worse, because naturally the windscreen wipers have packed up again! Damn it! You only just had the thing inspected by the Toaster Testing Authority! CRUNCH! There we go again. Look away for one second and some stuck-up marzipan-potato jockey cuts you off! "His fault!" you think as your head goes through the windscreen. Then the lights go out... When you come round, you're back where you took that puff, with a truly thunderous headache. Man! What was IN that stuff?

replacements.text: All right, have it your way. Heroically, you throw yourself onto your sword. Nothing happens! No blood, no pain, absolutely nothing! Frustrated, you try again. Still nothing. On your third attempt, you finally hit the target: yourself. You writhe on the ground in your death throes, without so much as a cry of pain. A true hero to the last! If only your girlfriend could see you now. You don't make an exit this stylish every day! Then it is over, and everything goes dark... Some time later, you wake to find yourself floating in a dark space. You shudder. Is this the afterlife? Is this really all there is? Not a bright prospect... Then you realise what woke you. A gentle voice drifts towards you, faint and distant. "Dave Parker!" it whispers. "You should know that no one can escape their destiny. Fleeing it is pointless: fate always catches up with you! Go and complete the tasks you have been given. By my divine authority, I grant you an extra life, and one more chance to fulfil your destiny..." As the voice fades, everything starts spinning. You grow dizzy and fall into a deep, dreamless sleep. When you open your eyes again, you are exactly where you tried to kill yourself...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: You continue beneath the thick, twisted branches of dead trees. Hardly a ray of sunlight gets through their bizarre crowns. Everything seems lifeless, filled with a ghostly emptiness. The edge of a swamp lies to the north. The path you arrived on leads west.
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: The ground is soft and boggy underfoot, and you have an uneasy feeling that something is about to happen. It's too quiet. Everything looks peaceful, certainly calm, but perhaps a little TOO peaceful...? The swamp lake lies to the north, and the enchanted forest stretches away to the south.
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: You reach a large swamp lake. This brown sludge is all that separates you from the island to the north. If King Richard's story is true, your destination lies behind the island's low hill: the royal castle, seized long ago by Zargon and his horde. From there, he directs the sinister schemes that have brought death and misery to the whole land. You can enter the swamp lake to the north, or head south, back towards the swamp and forest.
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: As you row across the lake, you look down at the brown sludge on either side. It reminds you unpleasantly of the coffee you brew at home before a long night. Six heaped spoonfuls per cup! Your "killer coffee" has had you topping the drug squad's wanted list for months, but you've never let that bother you. The stuff could raise the dead, then send them straight back to the afterlife with a heart attack! Not a bad comparison, actually. Who knows what's lurking beneath this brown mess, just waiting to come back to life...? Stop thinking and ROW! North, if you want to reach the island in one piece.
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: Curiosity leads you into the dense swamp. The ground is dangerously soft and slippery, but you press on until you have to admit you're hopelessly lost. Again. Furious, you fight through the wet vegetation, looking for a landmark, but all you do is go round in circles. At last, inspiration strikes: walk in a straight line! You'll reach the island's shore eventually, then follow it back to your boat. Encouraged, you push on until you reach a little clearing. To the southeast you can see the southern shore, where that strange sign stood. The one you didn't understand. "Phew, made it!" You start to crouch down for a breather, then realise with horror that you're already knee-deep in the ground! You kick frantically, but instead of getting out, you sink deeper. Like every proper adventure, "Soul Crystal" has a quicksand location. Now you know where it is! As you settle into your new career as a bog body, take comfort in the fact that your foot has just touched the remains of another unfortunate adventurer who chose the same route...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: You reach the shore of a lovely, peaceful island. Everything is wild and untouched, as though nobody has set foot here for centuries... "Damn! Not another parallel world!" you think, silently cursing certain game designers' lack of imagination. The swamp lake is behind you to the south. A wooded hill to the north should offer a good view. On your left, a sign reads: "Danger - quicksand! No entry! Parents are responsible for their children!" Perhaps you should save your game before exploring any farther...?
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: You enter an elderly hermit's hut, patched together over the years from the stones and branches scattered around the island. Since you didn't bother knocking, the old man looks up from sharpening arrowheads for his next wolf hunt. His curious, slightly vacant stare suggests he's wondering what planet you're from. Through the little doorway to the east, you can see the clearing outside.
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: You are in a small clearing in a dark forest. Stones, planks and other building materials litter the ground outside a hut to the west. A thin plume of smoke curls peacefully from its chimney. To the north, a steaming bog lies at the forest's edge, sending heavy, ominous banks of mist among the trees. A path on your right leads back up the hill, where you could get a better view of the island. Behind you stands a sign: "Danger - quicksand! No entry! Parents are responsible for their children!" If you've had the foresight to draw a map, now might be a good time to use it. If not, never mind. You'll understand what I mean when the time comes. Until then, remember to save regularly...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: With heroic effort, you drag yourself to the top of the hundred-metre hill. You sit on a rock to recover from your exhausting summit expedition, then survey the view. Dense forest surrounds the hill, with three paths winding through it. The western path descends to a clearing and the bog in the northwest of the island. The southern path leads to the lake shore, where your boat waits. To the north looms the dark, imposing destination of your long journey: Zargon's castle!
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: Still trembling from your narrow escape, you stop at the western edge of the bog to catch your breath. There's no sign of your pursuers. You've lost them! But where now? "Damn it!" you think bitterly. "Why didn't I stay in my cosy hotel and relax for a few weeks? I had to go looking for adventure, didn't I? Now look at me: stranded in the middle of nowhere with a pack of snapping zombies behind me! This whole game was a waste of money. I'll never buy rubbish like this again!" Just how right that last statement is becomes clear when you look around. The only way out is east, straight back to the zombies. They stopped chasing you for a reason: they know this bog very well. Sooner or later, it will be your grave...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: The path through the bog runs from south to west, though it owes more to your imagination than to anything underfoot. Your feet sink deeper into the spongy ground. Dense, damp mist rises on either side, taking the shapes of grotesque creatures that send shivers down your spine. Nonsense, you tell yourself. Just frayed nerves and an overactive imagination. After everything you've survived, it'll take more than a bit of fog and some spooky noises to frighten Dave Parker! You're about to press on with renewed courage when a strange bubbling noise comes from ahead, growing closer and closer. THAT is no figment of your imagination. You look around wildly, but the rolling fog hides the source of those dreadful sounds. They seem to rise from the deepest part of the bog...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: Before you stands your destination: Zargon's ruined castle! Little remains of the former royal palace. The only intact structure among the sorry ruins is an enormous gateway in the high wall before you. Rather discouragingly, it seems to be the only way into Zargon's headquarters. You can try entering his stronghold, if you dare. Nobody would blame you for thinking better of it and returning to your boat on the southern shore, though. There are some very unpleasant things behind those walls...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: You enter the gatehouse through which everyone visiting the king's castle once had to pass. You chuckle at the thought of the deaf old "gatekeeper" from "Mary's Inn" sitting here, inspecting the visitors. A thick layer of dust covers everything. Even so, I suspect the usual rabble got here first and carried off anything that wasn't nailed down. A small door in the east wall leads back outside, to the castle gate.
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: The enormous, iron-bound castle gate looms before you. It seems to grin down maliciously: "You're never getting out again!" An unpleasant little feeling tells you that you may only pass through this entrance once. You still have time to reconsider. In fairness, we ought to warn you: although you're on the right track, once you enter this gloomy pile you won't sleep until you've finished the game. So brew a few barrels of coffee, buy a few cartons of cigarettes, and above all think up some convincing excuses for your boss! Still got the courage, or the poor judgement, to enter Zargon's castle? Here are the exits. West leads to a small gatehouse, where you might find a last-minute clue or useful object. North takes you into the ruins, or headfirst into solid oak, depending on whether the gate is open. You could also retreat south, away from the castle, though that won't do much to complete your mission, will it?
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: Hmm... I know some people swear by mud baths, but this is a deep swamp, not a harmless spa treatment! You sink helplessly to the bottom of the lake, where you'll be preserved for all eternity. Personally, I think preserving yourself with the "Save" command would have been rather healthier...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: After a few paces, you stop and listen to the deceptive silence. No, you weren't imagining it. Something is moving beneath the constant bubbling of the bog. Footsteps approach from behind, slow but relentless. You whirl round, but see only thick mist twisting into grotesque faces that seem to mock your fear. Suddenly the ground beside you begins to boil. A horribly disfigured face breaks the surface: a half-rotted corpse! Frozen with horror, you watch a zombie drag itself from the depths. As you regain control of your limbs, its claws shoot towards your throat! Somehow you fling yourself aside in time, but stumble and land hard in the mud. The undead creature seems to have won. While you struggle to your feet, it staggers closer, hissing and snarling. Its jaws creak open and shut, exposing the revolting brown stumps of its teeth...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: Sorry. You had a real chance to escape with nothing worse than a fright, but you hesitated too long. The delighted zombie pulls you close and sinks its teeth into your young, tender flesh! Still, don't despair. You've fallen victim to a true gourmet. Some of your tastier parts, eyes, tongue and similar delicacies, will doubtless be taken to its store-cave and preserved. Unfortunate adventurers stray out here far too rarely to waste such a feast in one sitting...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: Coming back after your last encounter was a fatal mistake. A whole pack of zombies waits to welcome you, advancing with jerky movements and fixed stares. Leading them is the one you only just escaped! This time you react much faster. You spin round and run for your life as fast as the soggy ground allows, straight into the arms of another zombie who hadn't quite caught up with the proceedings. A shame, really. You were on course for a world record! Your new acquaintance is delighted. It hasn't had fresh meat in weeks, and a diet of bog-preserved adventurers gets a bit monotonous, even for a half-rotten stomach. After saying a quick grace, it gratefully sinks its teeth into you. "Damn! Who knew those brown stumps could still be so sharp?" is your last thought before everything blurs...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: As you head south out of the enchanted forest, the amulet that protected you on your way through the magical barrier snags on a dead branch. Without your noticing, it slips from your neck. You stroll cheerfully through the boundary between the two stretches of forest and emerge on the other side of the magical wall nicely browned, but unfortunately quite dead...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: Walking beneath the dead trees, you suddenly feel a vicious tug at your neck! Terrified, you thrash about, trying to shake off your invisible attacker. At last it lets go, and you nearly burst into hysterical laughter. Your "attacker" was your own amulet, caught on a branch. It now dangles from the tree as if mocking you...
replacements.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

replacements.text: Well, let's call that an attempt and leave it there. It wasn't much of a success, as you discover rather painfully. Before you can slip beneath the archway, something rattles down from above. For once, let's keep this brief: stepping on the little platform triggered the portcullis, which crushed you in one almighty blow! You're dead. Yes, really. You've kicked the bucket, bitten the dust, shuffled off this mortal coil. Gone! Don't complain to us. If you'd paid attention, you might have noticed the platform beneath the gate. So having to start again is rather more your fault than ours, isn't it? What's that? You don't believe me? Well, I can't say I blame you. You have no reason to. Perhaps this will convince you...:
